audit: Manual to Firmware Traceability (Performing Rigs AutoPilot + Remote)
scope_note: Documentation/reconciliation pass only. Joins docs/ui/user-guide-workflows.md and docs/ui/action-command-map.md to the established four-firmware behavioral contract. Does not perform new reverse engineering.

requirements.manual_action: Power on AutoPilot (connect 48V DC)
requirements.manual_claim: [user manual] AutoPilot has a status LED and power button; unit becomes operational on connect.
requirements.autopilot_firmware_path: Reset_Handler -> clock/peripheral init -> startup reference/input routine gated on PA22 -> radio-ID probe -> sketch_setup()'s internal MC4-wait loop
requirements.autopilot_state_effect: Boot proceeds; MC4-wait loop runs until MC4 received
requirements.hardware_effect: Full clock-tree/analog-block bring-up (MCLK/GCLK/OSCCTRL/OSC32KCTRL/SUPC/NVMCTRL/CMCC/AC/ADC0/ADC1/DAC/USB), concretely reproduced boot-to-steady-state
requirements.observable_result: Status LED state (unresolved), device responds to Remote queries once MC4 received
requirements.replacement_requirement: Replacement must reproduce the same boot-to-MC4-wait gating shape; startup reference/input routine's real-world PA22 purpose needs a product decision if reproduced verbatim.
requirements.external_unknown: PA22 physical signal identity (preserved, not solved here)

requirements.wire_behavior: '&|' -> 'V01R39'; bulk mode-0x62 push attempt (empty on cold boot, see MAN-RECONNECT-001); MC4 unconditionally
requirements.autopilot_firmware_path: ascii_dispatcher (0x8258) handles '&' and 'C'/'M' branches as for any sender
requirements.autopilot_state_effect: pending[5] set/consumed; MC4 clears 0x20000060 if this is the AutoPilot's first MC4
requirements.observable_result: Remote firmware-version field populates; AutoPilot may unlock main-loop if MC4 lands
requirements.replacement_requirement: Replacement AutoPilot must accept an unsolicited '&|'/'S|' probe and a possible bulk-push/MC4 immediately after Remote power-on.

requirements.manual_action: (supporting fact) per-channel STEP/DIR/driver-control GPIO identity
requirements.manual_claim: Not a manual action -- hardware mapping underlying MAN-MANUAL-003 and MAN-QUICKSETUP motor operation.

requirements.manual_action: Rotate jog wheel
requirements.manual_claim: [user manual s.4.1/5] motor moves continuously in the rotated direction; speed centered around zero.
requirements.remote_ui_behavior: Real velocity-sensitive quadrature encoder (SAMD51 EIC pins 0x31/0x32), callback FUN_00007de8
requirements.remote_firmware_path: FUN_0000de3c loop calls FUN_0000be94 every UI pump tick
requirements.wire_behavior: 0xF0 (mode 1) or 0xE0 (mode 2, selected when *0x200018e7==3) <len><0xFFx4>[<channel nibble><sign+23-bit value>]*<'|'><seq>; sent EVERY tick including idle/zero-record heartbeats
requirements.autopilot_firmware_path: ascii_dispatcher checks 0xF0/0xE0 before any ASCII branch; compares value against 0x20000180[channel] threshold; under threshold -> FUN_00005448(channel,value); at/over threshold -> FUN_00005274(channel,4). 0xE0 additionally maintains a per-channel latch (0x20001fdd/0x20001fe4/0x20001ff4) suppressing a REPEAT at-limit call once already latched.
requirements.autopilot_state_effect: Per-channel jog/at-limit state per the above; 0xE0's latch state persists across deliveries until reset by a value change
requirements.hardware_effect: Feeds the same real timer/ISR/GPIO step-pulse mechanism G/I use (MAN-MOTORCFG-005 pins)
requirements.observable_result: Motor moves in real time, proportional to jog input
requirements.retry_timeout_behavior: None -- unconditional per-tick send; stop is implicit (MAN-MANUAL-003). No proven AutoPilot-side dead-man/frame-loss timeout exists for either 0xF0 or 0xE0.
requirements.replacement_requirement: Replacement must implement both 0xF0 and 0xE0 with byte-identical record layout, the 0xE0 at-limit-suppression latch, and must NOT invent a dead-man timeout not present in the vendor firmware.
requirements.external_unknown: which specific UI screen sets *0x200018e7==3 (selecting 0xE0); exact RAM source of the jog frame's own channel nibble (plausibly *0x2000180c, not independently confirmed)

requirements.autopilot_state_effect: Whatever state the last-received 0xF0/0xE0 record left
requirements.observable_result: Motor stops (implicit -- no proven AutoPilot dead-man timeout was found, so behavior depends entirely on the last delivered frame plus whatever downstream motion-profile logic already governs move completion)
requirements.replacement_requirement: Replacement must treat 'no new frame arrives' as the sole stop signal, matching vendor behavior exactly (do not add a timeout not present in the original).

requirements.manual_action: (background) Remote boot triggers bulk program re-arm
requirements.manual_claim: Not a discrete user action -- a connection-health event.
requirements.remote_firmware_path: FUN_0000c440's tail: loop every channel with nonzero local-record data, send '+' mode=0x62, then unconditionally MC4
requirements.wire_behavior: '+' mode=0x62 (confirm1=confirm2=1) per nonzero-data channel, then MC4<...>| for all channels
requirements.autopilot_firmware_path: Same '+' handler as interactive '+' (MAN-AUTO-002), but mode=0x62 (>50) DOES cross the compute+persist threshold
requirements.autopilot_state_effect: FUN_00004ca8 computes target=start+delta per channel; FUN_000043f0 persists the whole struct to the flash-backed buffer -- concretely proven end to end through a real G-mode-1 move-commit
requirements.observable_result: A previously-recorded Auto-Mode program becomes drivable (target armed) without any further user action
requirements.persistence_effect: Real, proven flash persistence (dirties the buffer; a subsequent save writes flash 0x12000)
requirements.retry_timeout_behavior: Gate: FUN_0000c440's own 'S|'->'P...' round trip succeeding cleanly within ~200 ticks (any response shape). Push loop additionally requires the UI-set flag 0x20000fa0 ('has real programmed data'), never set by boot itself -- so a literal cold boot's push is EMPTY (only MC4 fires).
requirements.replacement_requirement: Replacement AutoPilot must expect this exact re-arm shape at every Remote boot (and MAN-RECONNECT-002); a cold-boot AutoPilot should NOT assume a nonzero target is present.

requirements.manual_action: Connect trigger cable before vs. after power-up (sensitivity behavior)
requirements.manual_claim: [user manual s.12] before power-up = noise baseline established, less sensitive/more noise-immune; after power-up = more sensitive, more prone to false triggers.
requirements.autopilot_firmware_path: Analog arm: exponentially-smoothed PB05/ADC1 filter (FUN_000042a4)
requirements.autopilot_state_effect: Blend coefficient (0x20000014) is permanently-zero .data; one-shot latch (0x20003118) never clears -- the very first (boot-time) sample is permanently latched for the whole power cycle
requirements.observable_result: A trigger chain already connected at power-up influences the one boot-time sample latched for the session; a transient occurring after boot cannot affect the analog path at all -- explains the manual's claim exactly.
requirements.replacement_requirement: Replacement can choose to reproduce this exact quirk (permanent first-sample latch) or design a proper continuously-resampled filter -- a product decision, not an evidence gap.

requirements.manual_action: Jog to first position, click to confirm
requirements.manual_claim: [firmware, CONFIRMED] position query gates a resend of LL1.
requirements.remote_ui_behavior: Jog phase (same 0xF0/0xE0 mechanism as MAN-MANUAL-002) then click
requirements.remote_firmware_path: FUN_0000b834 sends I9|/I1| (selected by *0x200018e7), waits ~1000-3000 ticks (6 retries)
requirements.wire_behavior: 0xF0/0xE0 jog stream, then I9| or I1|, then 'LL1|'x3 IF the query succeeds
requirements.autopilot_firmware_path: Same 0xF0/0xE0 receiver as MAN-MANUAL-002; I9/I1 via the same I-family handler
requirements.autopilot_state_effect: I1 completes normally (aliases channel 0); I9 is a genuine dead end (out-of-bounds channel index 8, never scheduled)
requirements.observable_result: 'Setting first / limit...' shown
requirements.retry_timeout_behavior: 6 retries, ~1000-3000 ticks total, then the query simply times out
requirements.replacement_requirement: Replacement need not make I9 succeed -- the Remote already discards its parsed result (0x200027f0 has zero readers anywhere in the image); the query's SUCCESS/FAILURE (not its value) is what gates the LL1 resend.

requirements.manual_action: (background) '!' bulk query response field-count mismatch
requirements.manual_claim: Not a discrete user action -- a protocol-level fact underlying MAN-INFO/status queries.
requirements.remote_firmware_path: 0xc440's parser calls its numeric-field parser exactly 10 times then unconditionally marks itself done
requirements.wire_behavior: '!0|'/'!1|' -> AutoPilot emits 11 comma-terminated fields; Remote consumes only 10
requirements.autopilot_firmware_path: 0x8c70 event-7 builder
requirements.autopilot_state_effect: Field 11 and its trailing comma are left byte-for-byte UNCONSUMED in the real RX ring buffer (confirmed by direct read/write-pointer inspection); no error, assert, or crash on either side.
requirements.observable_result: Silent, both sides
requirements.replacement_requirement: This is a documented, genuine firmware discrepancy. This pass records the behavior only -- whether a replacement preserves the 11-field emission or the 10-field consumption is a product decision, not resolved here.

requirements.manual_action: (background) I9 out-of-range dead end
requirements.manual_claim: Not a discrete user action -- a protocol-level fact underlying MAN-LIMITS-002.
requirements.autopilot_firmware_path: RX handler decodes channel digit '9' to array index 8
requirements.autopilot_state_effect: A real out-of-bounds scratch-RAM write occurs (confirmed live), but channel_event_monitor's scan loop only ever visits indices 0-3, so event 15 is never scheduled
requirements.observable_result: Remote's query simply times out with no error surfaced
